newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: WTO chief in Seoul, "frugality campaign" on agenda.
newsitem.headline: WTO chief in Seoul, "frugality campaign" on agenda.

text.p: The head of the World Trade Organisation arrived in South Korea on Tuesday amid a simmering dispute between Seoul and its major Western trading partners over an anti-import campaign.
Renato Ruggiero, director-general of the WTO, is scheduled to meet ministers of trade, finance and foreign affairs during his four-day visit.

The European Union and the United States have attacked South Korea's government over what they call its complicity in an "austerity campaign" targeting foreign consumer goods, including cars, spirits and cosmetics.
They complain the campaign, combined with official red tape slowing imports, conflicts with WTO free-trade principals.

"During Mr Ruggiero's visit, we will try to clarify misunderstandings caused by U.S. and EU insistence that South Korea's frugality campaign is led by the government," a trade ministry official told Reuters.
The frugality drive kicked in last year after President Kim Young-sam urged Koreans to cut back spending on luxury goods to reduce a snowballing trade deficit.
Civic and religious groups, backed by the media, have embraced the campaign. Foreign-made furs, golf clubs and even household appliances have been blacklisted.
In the past, the government openly ran anti-import crusades to improve the country's terms of trade.
Ruggiero is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on President Kim on Wednesday.
He leaves for China on Friday to discuss Beijing's decade-long quest to join the WTO.
